## Natural history notes

A medium-sized dung-loving mushroom characterized by a pale gray to whitish cap, dark gills that become blackish as the spores mature, and a slender whitish stem. In Florida, it is most often found in warm, humid pastures, grassy fields, and livestock areas where it grows directly from dung or dung-enriched soil. It helps decompose animal waste and recycle nutrients, and while it may resemble other dung-associated mushrooms, it should not be consumed because similar species can be difficult to distinguish.
